findings.failure_path: model_family('openai/house-model') returns codex solely from the provider alias, although the actual model's family is unknown. With implementer-family claude, this OpenAI-compatible endpoint can serve Claude and still produce an accepted independent verdict. Kimi similarly falls back from an unknown explicit model to provider or alias words.
findings.smallest_fix: Resolve the effective model ID, including model-table overrides, and skip unrecognized families. Provider and alias names must not establish independence for an unknown explicit model.

findings.failure_path: Valid TOML can define default_model="kimi-review" and, under [models], kimi-review={model="claude-sonnet-4-5", provider="proxy"}. The private config retains this definition, but family resolution only recognizes a literal [models.kimi-review] header. It finds no model, infers kimi from the alias, and allows the configured Claude model to review a Claude implementation.
findings.smallest_fix: Parse TOML structurally and resolve the selected model from the parsed models mapping. Add coverage for inline model tables.

findings.failure_path: kimi_config reads config A into kept, then filter_toml rereads the file for family resolution. If an atomic update changes alias review from Claude to DeepSeek between those reads, eligibility uses DeepSeek while launch writes config A and runs Claude. A clean response can therefore pass as independent for a Claude implementer.
findings.smallest_fix: Read the config once and derive both eligibility and launch configuration from that same in-memory snapshot; test replacement between the current read points.
